rounds.text: Mufin Green Finance is demonstrating exceptional operational momentum, evidenced by a compounded profit growth of 153% [E15] and sales growth of 40% [E14] over the trailing twelve months. This performance significantly outpaces the sector median profit growth of 22.3% and sales growth of 17.4% [E64, E65], suggesting the company is capturing market share at an aggressive rate. The market has recognized this trajectory, as the stock maintains a strong technical position, trading near its 52-week high [E35] and holding above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E36]. Furthermore, the company’s ability to attract foreign institutional interest, which has grown from 0.00% to 1.80% since late 2023 [E28], indicates a broadening base of investor confidence. While the company faces liquidity challenges with negative operating cash flow [E21, E22], it maintains a comfortable short-term liquidity position with a current ratio of 4.01x [E25]. Conceded: the company trades at a premium valuation with a P/E of 60.4x [E1] and a negative margin of safety [E32], and institutional money flow is currently negative [E30].

Mufin Green Finance Ltd is currently trading at a significant valuation premium that is disconnected from its underlying financial performance. The stock commands a P/E ratio of 72.24x against a sector benchmark of 18.72x [E6], while its price-to-book ratio of 4.89x sits well above the sector average of 1.25x [E7]. This aggressive pricing is further challenged by a discounted cash flow analysis that suggests an intrinsic value of only Rs 54 per share, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -166.3% [E31, E32]. The company’s operational efficiency remains lackluster, evidenced by a median return on equity of only 7% over the last three years [E19, E49]. Furthermore, the firm faces severe cash flow issues, reporting negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -695 Cr and Rs -699 Cr respectively in March 2026 [E22, E23]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong compounded sales growth of 40% and profit growth of 153% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. Despite these growth figures, the combination of institutional outflows [E30, E60] and a reduction in promoter holdings by 10.88 percentage points since December 2023 [E27] signals a lack of long-term confidence from key stakeholders.

Conceded: the company trades at a rich P/E of 72.24x against the sector benchmark of 18.72x [E6], and a P/B of 4.89x against 1.25x [E7], alongside a DCF intrinsic value calculation of Rs 54 leaving a negative margin of safety [E31, E32]. However, the bear's dismissal of operational efficiency and cash flow misses the explosive growth reality: compounded sales growth is 40% and compounded profit growth reaches an exceptional 153% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. This exceptional earnings expansion is further reinforced by sector comparison, where the company's ROCE of 8% outperforms the sector benchmark of 5.66% [E10] and significantly beats the sector median ROCE of 6.1% [E66]. Furthermore, the bear highlights institutional outflow [E30, E60] and promoter reduction [E27], but overlooks the vital counter-trend that foreign institutions have increased their holdings by 1.80 percentage points since December 2023 [E28]. Conceded: median return on equity stands at a modest 7% [E19, E49], but results are rapidly improving with the earnings profile scoring 67 out of 100 and a positive flag that the company is expected to deliver a good quarter [E45, E62].

Conceded: compounded sales growth is 40% and compounded profit growth reaches 153% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15], and foreign institutions have increased holdings by 1.80 percentage points since December 2023 [E28]. However, that explosive growth sits on top of catastrophic operational reality: operating cash flow collapsed to negative ₹695 Cr and free cash flow to negative ₹699 Cr in March 2026, driving a cash conversion of -24.82x [E21, E22, E23]. Conceded: ROCE outperforms some sector benchmarks at 8% [E10], but the core profitability remains low with a median return on equity of just 7% [E19] and a low interest coverage ratio [E48]. Furthermore, citing an expected good quarter [E45] ignores that earnings growth is decelerating [E57] and working capital days have ballooned from 39.7 to 108 days [E51]. The heavy reliance on a high P/E of 72.24x [E6] and a negative margin of safety (-166.3%) [E32] leaves the valuation completely unjustified by the evidence.
